text:
Anna S (Support): Hey team — Escalating a Solara customer issue. They claim they set a 365-day custom retention via API on 2024-10-28 but objects are still showing the org default (90d) and are scheduled for deletion next week. Ticket: https://redwood.support/t/4782. Customer says delete occurred on 2024-11-01 but objects remained visible via search.

Marco (eng-infra): Can you paste a couple of object IDs and the tenant id? Also, did they recently migrate accounts or we run any tenant-wide policy rollouts?

Anna S (Support): Tenant: tenant_solara. Two sample objects: obj_9a7b2c, obj_4f1d0e. Metadata GET shows retention_days: 90. Customer provided a screenshot claiming they PATCHed "retention_days: 365" on 2024-10-28. Example metadata response: 
```
{
  "id": "obj_9a7b2c",
  "tenant": "tenant_solara",
  "retention_days": 90,
  "created_at": "2024-07-18T12:34:56Z"
}
```

Priya (security): Do we have an audit log entry for the PATCH? Check KMS/HSM rotation window as well — if the policy change was performed with a disabled key, it may not have been committed. Also post the API request if you have it (no full keys).

retention-bot: automated check: no tenant-wide retention policy change recorded for tenant_solara between 2024-10-20 and 2024-11-05.

Marco (eng-infra): Okay. Two likely paths: (1) the PATCH never persisted and client saw a 200 due to a response bug, or (2) policy persisted but the delete worker applied default fallback because the backfill job didn't run. Can you run our diagnostic and paste output: `tools/backfill-check --tenant tenant_solara`

Anna S (Support): Ran it, output below:
```
backfill_check: last_run: 2024-11-02T03:12:01Z
backfill_status: completed
delete_worker: last_processed_queue_item: obj_2c3d4e (2024-11-03T22:01:09Z)
policy_diff: tenant_policy: NOT_FOUND, object_metadata_policy: 90
```

Marco (eng-infra): Interesting — backfill ran but reports tenant_policy NOT_FOUND. That aligns with retention-bot. Priya, could KMS deny the commit? Any KMS errors around 2024-10-28 in audit logs?

Priya (security): I checked quick glance, there is a KMS rotation activity on 2024-10-27 23:58 UTC for key rk-prod-7. I don't see a corresponding policy-change log tied to tenant_solara. Recommend: (A) run `audit/export --tenant tenant_solara --start 2024-10-27 --end 2024-10-29` and attach to the ticket, (B) SRE to grep API gateway logs for a 200 on PATCH /v1/tenants/tenant_solara/retention.

Steph (legal): We need to preserve the currently visible objects while this is investigated. Please apply a preservation hold for tenant_solara immediately and provide a list of object ids to preserve. We will want an export for legal review.

Marco (eng-infra): I can temporarily set a retention override (server-side) for tenant_solara to 365 while infra investigates. Command (admin):
```
POST /admin/tenants/tenant_solara/retention 
Authorization: Bearer <admin>
Body: { "retention_days": 365, "reason": "legal-preserve-solara-4782" }
```
I will only apply it if support confirms legal asked.

Anna S (Support): Confirmed — Steph asked for preservation. Opening support ticket now and attaching diagnostics + the two object ids. Ticket will request SRE to run API gateway grep and infra to apply admin override if appropriate.

Priya (security): Also note: if there was an attempted PATCH that failed to persist because of a transient DB error, we may still have an entry in the request logs but no commit event. SRE, please check DB write errors near 2024-10-28T00:00-01:00UTC.

Marco (eng-infra): Adding to my queue. I'll post updates in this thread after grep. If we find the PATCH and no commit, we'll reapply the change and trigger a backfill for affected objects.

Anna S (Support): Thanks — I'll keep the customer informed and confirm once the legal export is ready. :thumbsup:
